applies_to: All undergraduates entering the College of Arts and Sciences
release_rule: Exemptions on the current Campus Living page: living with parents or guardians within 30 miles, married, 21 or older at the start of fall semester, or a new transfer with 61 credits. Semesters on approved overseas programs count toward the requirement.
change_note: Raised from four semesters to six.
notes: Six semesters is the new requirement as stated by the college. The undergraduate catalog, the Campus Living page and the 2026-27 housing agreement read on November 19, 2026 still describe a four-semester requirement, so the source link points to the current exemptions page.

applies_to: Full-time undergraduates under 21 in their first and second years
release_rule: Released after four full semesters in university housing or at age 21, whichever comes first. Married students and those living with a parent or guardian locally may request an exemption.
notes: Upper-division housing is not guaranteed; the housing office focuses its beds on students under the requirement.

applies_to: Students who began at Reed in fall 2021 or later as first-year students
release_rule: Typical exemptions: living with family within about 30 miles, married or with children, 24 or older, veterans, Title IX or disability-related approvals. First-year or sophomore transfers live on campus one year; junior and senior transfers are exempt.
notes: Two-year guarantee and requirement adopted for the class entering fall 2021; measured as four semesters from enrollment, and study abroad does not change the count.

applies_to: All full-time undergraduates in their first and second years
release_rule: Class year is based on total academic years in college. Exemptions are handled by the Office of Residence Life.
notes: The university encourages students to stay on campus all four years but requires only two.

applies_to: All new students, first-year and transfer, for their first two academic years
release_rule: Exceptions for married students, students with children, students 21 or older, and dependents of Puget Sound employees. Transfers who lived on campus elsewhere may appeal after one year.
notes: Over 70 percent of students choose university housing each year.

applies_to: Single undergraduates under 21 who have not yet lived on campus four semesters
release_rule: Released after four semesters on campus (transfer semesters count), at age 21, or if married or with children. Petitions to live off campus are made the semester before.
change_note: College-owned housing is no longer required for juniors and seniors as of 2026-27.
notes: Sources conflict: the catalog's student life page says all students live in college-owned housing for eight semesters, while the Residence Life junior/senior FAQ says college-owned housing is not required for juniors and seniors as of 2026-27. The Residence Life page was treated as current.

applies_to: Willamette College (Salem campus) students; PNCA students in Portland live on for two semesters
release_rule: Released automatically after four semesters in a residence hall. Exceptions for married or partnered students and students living with parents or guardians within 30 miles; other requests by petition.

applies_to: All full-time students, first-year through senior
release_rule: Commuters living at home are exempt. A limited number of students are released to live off campus each year, set by enrollment and housing inventory.
notes: Four-year residency requirement stated in the Residential Guidebook; students may also live in college-affiliated fraternity houses.

applies_to: All students through their third (junior) year
release_rule: Exemptions for married students, students with children, students 23 or older, and students under 16. The Petition Committee can release sophomores and juniors for health, financial hardship, or living at a parent's home within 30 miles.
notes: Kalamazoo runs on quarters; three academic years is shown as six semesters. Sources conflict: the Residence Life requirements page (updated August 12, 2026) requires juniors to live on campus, while the catalog's student life policies page still says juniors are not required. The Residence Life page was treated as current.

applies_to: All enrolled students, for the duration of their studies
release_rule: No categories are listed; any exception needs prior written approval from Residential Life and the Dean of Students.
notes: Students must also be on the college dining plan and may not use non-Kenyon housing to supplement college housing.

applies_to: Students who start as first-years, for their first three years
release_rule: A limited number of rising juniors are approved each year to live off campus (mostly in Greek or athletic houses). Transfer students are not required to live on campus.
notes: Seniors are not guaranteed housing and apply if they want to stay.

applies_to: All unmarried, full-time undergraduates under 24 at admission
release_rule: Six consecutive full semesters in college housing with a meal plan. Married students may be exempted; transfers live on campus until they reach the requirement (prior residency may count). Admission may approve exemptions for new first-years only before they are bound by the contract.

applies_to: No on-campus housing requirement found
release_rule: n/a
notes: The handbook's 'residency requirement' is academic: two consecutive years of full-time study at the Bronxville campus, plus the junior or senior year there. No rule requiring students to live in college housing was found in the handbook or Residential Life pages; the handbook's housing section could not be read in full, so this is a moderate-confidence finding.

applies_to: First-year and sophomore students
release_rule: Juniors and seniors may apply to live off campus through housing selection. First-years and sophomores may appeal if 22 or older, married, with family within 30 miles, with children, or for financial, accessibility, leave or study-abroad reasons.

applies_to: All enrolled students
release_rule: Approved exemption: parents' or guardians' home within a 45-mile drive (student lives there). Other extenuating circumstances reviewed case by case each year.
notes: About 95 percent of students live on campus all four years.

applies_to: All students for their entire time at Union, provided space is available
release_rule: Commuters living with a parent or guardian within 30 miles may apply. A senior off-campus release lottery frees about 10 to 20 students a year.
notes: Union runs on trimesters; four years is shown as eight semesters.

applies_to: All undergraduates, for their first four semesters at Clark
release_rule: Exceptions granted by Residential Life and Housing; incoming students appeal through Admissions. Transfers entering as juniors or seniors are not required to live on campus; on-campus semesters elsewhere can count by appeal.

applies_to: All full-time, enrolled undergraduates during their years of study
release_rule: Students may apply for commuter status if living with a parent or family member within 50 miles.
notes: A third-party college directory describes the requirement as through junior year; Drew's own housing page states all years.

applies_to: Students in their first two years at SPU
release_rule: Not assigned housing if they graduated high school two or more years earlier or take fewer than nine credits a quarter. Other exemptions by yearly petition; financial exceptions only for severe hardship.
notes: SPU runs on quarters; two academic years is shown as four semesters.

applies_to: All full-time undergraduates until they have 85 credit hours
release_rule: Students with 85 or more credit hours may live off campus. Commuters living with a parent, guardian, spouse or child are exempt; married students and single parents are also excepted.
notes: The rule is credit-based; 85 credits is reached at about the end of the third year, so it is shown as six semesters.

applies_to: All undergraduates, including transfer and international students, for their first three years
release_rule: Students meeting listed criteria (for example, living with family locally or on an approved away program) may request an exemption. Housing after the third year is not guaranteed.
notes: Stetson says it has had a three-year requirement for more than a decade.

applies_to: First- and second-year students under 21, including those with AP or Running Start credit
release_rule: Exceptions are rare and case by case: marriage or family obligations, medical or disability needs, pregnancy, or living with family within 20 miles. Transfers with third- or fourth-year standing are not covered.
notes: Seattle University runs on quarters; two academic years is shown as four semesters.

applies_to: All first-year, sophomore and junior students (students entering fall 2024 or later)
release_rule: Exemptions include living with a parent within about 25 miles, two prior years of full-time college or junior standing (56 credits), age 22 by the start of fall, veterans, and away programs.
change_note: Raised from two years to three for students entering fall 2024.

applies_to: Forest Grove undergraduates, for four full fall and spring semesters
release_rule: Exemptions (granted a year at a time) include age and living locally with family; study abroad and prior college semesters count toward the four.
notes: A full meal plan is also required until the requirement is met.

applies_to: All undergraduate students
release_rule: Exceptions: living with a parent, guardian or sibling within 30 driving miles; age 23 or older; married; veterans; legal guardians of minors; approved accessibility exemptions. No credit-hour release.

applies_to: Students for their first three years
release_rule: Eligible to live off campus after three years (six semesters) in university housing, at age 23, commuting from a parent's home within 30 miles, with a bachelor's degree, veterans, or married and living with a spouse locally. Approvals are annual.

applies_to: First-year and sophomore students, beginning with the class entering fall 2026
release_rule: Sophomore exemptions mirror the first-year process: married, partnered or parenting; veterans or non-traditional students; primary caregivers; high financial need with a parent within 15 miles; medical or disability needs.
change_note: Sophomore live-on requirement added for the class entering fall 2026 (previously first year only).

applies_to: No requirement
release_rule: n/a
notes: The housing FAQ says first-year students are not required to live on campus at this time, though it is encouraged; on-campus residents can receive a housing grant.

applies_to: No requirement found
release_rule: n/a
notes: Neither the 2026-27 housing contract nor the Residential Life pages state a live-on requirement; admissions material says nearly 90 percent of first-year students live on campus. Moderate confidence.

applies_to: Full-time undergraduates until they reach 90 earned credits (students entering fall 2027 or later); 60 credits for earlier entrants
release_rule: Release categories: age 22, the credit threshold, marriage, living with a parent within 30 miles, required away placements, study abroad, and special circumstances.
change_note: Credit threshold for release rises from 60 to 90 for students entering fall 2027.
notes: The rule is credit-based; 90 credits is reached at about the end of the third year, so it is shown as six semesters (four under the 60-credit rule for current students).

applies_to: All full-time students admitted fall 2024 or later
release_rule: May live off campus after completing four full semesters at PLU (study away counts) or reaching age 20, when living at home with a parent in Pierce County or approved zip codes, or when living with a spouse or child.
notes: New requirement effective for students admitted from fall 2024; earlier entrants follow the rule in force at their admit term.

applies_to: All College of Arts and Sciences undergraduates, for the duration of their undergraduate experience
release_rule: Exemptions: living with a parent within 30 miles, under 16 or 23 or older, part-time enrollment, married or with a dependent, and transfers living with a parent within 60 miles. Other cases by off-campus petition.

applies_to: Resident students entering fall 2023 or later, for four years (transfers included)
release_rule: Commuters living in a parent's or guardian's primary residence within 35 miles are exempt.
change_note: Raised to four years for students entering fall 2023 (from a three-year rule).

applies_to: First- and second-year students, and transfers with under two years of college
release_rule: Exemptions: commuting from a parent's home within 40 miles, married, dependents, independent or over 21, veterans, transfers with over two years, medical needs, study abroad, under 12 credits, under 17, medical leave.
